note: Item wording comes from the deposit's own label file, data-clean/normdat-labels.csv, which keys text to IDs of the form mv.<INSTRUMENT>.<FACET><n>. The response columns in study1-maindat.csv are it.<INSTRUMENT>.<FACET><n> -- the same instrument, facet and number, differing only in the rater-frame prefix, mv for the norming ratings and it for the informant-target ratings this table holds. Stata's `import delimited` cannot keep dots in variable names, which is how it.MCQ.F1 becomes the live code itmcqf1; data/sun_2025_morality.do then applies `rename *, lower`. The code is therefore the source column name with dots stripped, a mechanical rename with the number preserved, and the prefix substitution is the only inference in the table. NO RESPONSE ANCHORS ARE PUBLISHED. resp runs 1-5 but neither the deposit nor the paper states what the five points were labelled: the two supplementary workbooks that would carry a codebook, study1-suppdat.xlsx and study2-suppdat.xlsx, are password-encrypted (their OLE2 containers hold EncryptedPackage and StrongEncryptionTransform streams), and the article itself is paywalled (doi:10.1037/pspp0000539 returns HTTP 403). option_text is therefore left empty rather than invented. The live table also carries a handful of NA resp values, which is response-data missingness rather than an item-text matter. The four items are the MCQ Fairness facet, and itmcqf3 ('doesn't believe it is important to treat others fairly') is the facet's only reverse-worded item, which is what verify_sun_2025_morality_study1_fairnessMCQ.R tests.
